# STEP manifest (generated - do not edit by hand)

Generated by `cad/step/manifest.py` from `_build_index.json` (what `build_step.py` wrote) and `_verify_results.json` (what `verify_step.py` measured by re-importing every file with CadQuery/OCCT). Re-run the three scripts to refresh.

## What these files are - and are not

* **Script-generated interchange geometry.** Every STEP file is produced by CadQuery 2.8 (OCCT B-rep) from the numbers in the OpenSCAD `*_params.scad` files (read programmatically by `scadparams.py`; no dimension is typed in the builders, except the few literals that sit inside module bodies of the .scad files, listed under *Limitations*).
* **Not native parametric CAD.** The files carry no sketches, no constraints, no feature tree and no spreadsheet. The native parametric models are the FreeCAD rebuild described in `cad/freecad/REBUILD_GUIDE.md` (see `cad/CAD_STATUS.md`).
* **Bought-in parts are simplified envelopes** (`*_envelope`); their sizes are the ASSUMED/class sizes already stated in `pf_bought.scad` and `cad/README.md` and must be re-checked against the purchased part's drawing. Fasteners, anchors, decals/tape and cable runs are not modelled.

## Verification summary

* Files: **89 part files + 16 assembly files = 105**. All re-imported from disk: **all solids valid (BRepCheck)**.
* **79** files were compared with an OpenSCAD STL of the same part/assembly in the same frame (volume, bounding box and corner position, and STEP-surface-to-STL-surface distance; thresholds: volume 2 %, bbox 2 % and >0.3 mm, surface agreement >= 99 % of sampled STEP surface within max(0.3 mm, 2.5 x STL sample spacing)). The other files have no OpenSCAD module that isolates them (plain boxes/cylinders, trimmed or merged bodies); they are validated for solid validity and volume against their closed-form parameters only.
* Printed parts are additionally compared with the checked-in `cad/stl/*.stl` (print orientation: volume only).
* Assembly volume comparison uses sum(body volumes) - sum(pairwise overlaps): the OpenSCAD STL is a boolean UNION, while the STEP assemblies keep separate bodies, some of which overlap in the source model (see *Interferences*).

### Files outside tolerance (all explained below the table)

| id | what differs |
|---|---|
| `occ_cover` | volume -12.49 % vs checked-in stl/occ_cover.stl  -> MODEL ISSUE: in the .scad the probe clamp boss and the LED seat are NOT connected to this shell (3 separate solids); exported as 3 parts |
| `gantry_antenna_arm_assy` | bbox X extent -32.00 mm  -> reference STL also contains the M8 pivot bolts and nylon spacers (hardware, not in STEP) |
| `gantry_assembly` | bbox X extent -32.00 mm; bbox Z extent -80.00 mm; bbox min-corner Z shifted +80.00 mm  -> reference STL additionally contains anchors, cross bolts, pivot bolts and conduit hardware; STEP has none |
| `barrier_rotor_assy` | volume -3.20 % vs OpenSCAD STL; bbox Y extent -5.00 mm; bbox Z extent -12.30 mm; only 98.8 % of STEP surface within 1.25 mm of OpenSCAD surface  -> reference STL also contains the M8 hinge bolt, 2 M6 clamp bolts, 2 M8 counterweight studs, red tape bands and a different (solid) inline tip cap |
| `barrier_photo_post_assy` | only 99.0 % of STEP surface within 1.25 mm of OpenSCAD surface  -> reference photo_post() draws a solid 24x24x6 cap instead of the printed hollow cap |
| `barrier_assembly` | bbox Y extent -12.30 mm; bbox min-corner Y shifted +12.30 mm  -> reference STL additionally has anchor nuts, hinge/clamp bolts, studs, decals, tape bands, beam line, solid inline caps |
| `occupancy_node_assy` | bbox Z extent -27.50 mm; bbox min-corner Z shifted +27.50 mm  -> reference STL also contains the 2 M5 countersunk screws |
| `lane_layout_assy` | bbox Z extent -80.00 mm; bbox min-corner Z shifted +80.00 mm  -> reference STL = the same three layout() placements run through OpenSCAD (hardware included in reference only). The gantry is MIRRORED (x -> -x) exactly as in the .scad, so handed parts are mirror-image copies. |

### Weldment cross-check against the sentence at the top of MATERIALS.md

MATERIALS.md says the CadQuery B-rep weldment volume is 1424.8 cm3 (11.2 kg). The weldment regenerated from the .scad (grout slots and cheek relief notches added, which the first CadQuery version omitted) is **1414.5 cm3 = 11.10 kg**. The 11.24 kg 'analytical sum' in MATERIALS.md is 7.68 + 2.43 + 1.13 and is itself a rounded-area estimate (`calcs.py` section 6), not a CAD number.

## Interferences (overlapping bodies in assemblies)

The OpenSCAD model unions everything, so overlaps are invisible there. In STEP assemblies they are real overlapping solids. Largest overlaps per assembly (pairwise common volume > 1 mm3; mm3):

* `gantry_antenna_arm_assy`: 1 overlapping pairs, total 0.50 cm3. tilt_plate / rfid_reader: 502.7
* `edge_internals_assy`: 6 overlapping pairs, total 125.38 cm3. smps_lrs150 / wire_trunking: 79528; din_device_6 / din_device_7: 11700; din_device_7 / din_device_8: 11700; din_device_8 / poe_switch: 11700; mount_plate_3mm_5052 / din_rail: 6432.3; buck_module / wire_trunking: 4320
* `edge_node_assy`: 11 overlapping pairs, total 139.15 cm3. smps_lrs150 / wire_trunking: 79528; din_device_6 / din_device_7: 11700; din_device_7 / din_device_8: 11700; din_device_8 / poe_switch: 11700; mount_plate_3mm_5052 / din_rail: 6432.3; heat_sink / sun_hood: 5760
* `gantry_assembly`: 20 overlapping pairs, total 182.21 cm3. smps_lrs150 / wire_trunking: 79528; socket_cheek_short_-x / cable_boot: 14245.8; din_device_6 / din_device_7: 11700; din_device_7 / din_device_8: 11700; din_device_8 / poe_switch: 11700; base_plate_16mm_MS / flexible_conduit: 7854
* `barrier_housing_assy`: 16 overlapping pairs, total 72.47 cm3. frame_post_-1-1 / front_panel: 20794.4; frame_post_+1-1 / front_panel: 20794.4; rail_x_z1_-1 / roof: 8238.6; rail_x_z1_-1 / front_panel: 6775.1; rail_x_z0_-1 / front_panel: 6775.1; rail_y_z1_+1 / roof: 2280.1
* `barrier_drive_train_assy`: 5 overlapping pairs, total 27.00 cm3. flange_bearing_rear / stub_shaft: 11309.7; flange_bearing_front / stub_shaft: 11309.7; gearmotor / jaw_coupling: 1608.2; jaw_coupling / stub_shaft: 1570.8; bearing_plate / flange_bearing_rear: 1206.4
* `barrier_rotor_assy`: 1 overlapping pairs, total 8.00 cm3. hub / counterweight_tail_bar: 8000

These are properties of the OpenSCAD source (bought-in envelopes drawn solid, DIN devices wider than their pitch, front panel placed inside the frame envelope, roof tilted into the frame, bolted lap joints) and were NOT silently removed from the STEP files.


## Per-file mismatch explanations

* **Reference hardware.** The OpenSCAD reference modules also draw fasteners, anchors, studs, decals and tape bands. STEP files contain fabricated parts and envelopes only, so assembly bounding boxes differ by the hardware overhang (see table at the top). Part-level files all agree within 1 %.
* **Overlaps.** Assembly volume is compared as sum of bodies minus pairwise overlap because OpenSCAD unions. Overlaps come from the .scad (envelopes drawn solid, DIN devices wider than pitch, front panel inside the frame).
* **Pole mass.** CAD pole 31.7 kg vs 12.96 kg in MATERIALS.md: the .scad T-slot profile is far more solid than the vendor 5.4 kg/m. This is a real inconsistency inside our model, not a STEP error.
* **occ_cover.** The .scad cover is three disconnected solids (shell, probe clamp boss, LED seat). Exported as three STEP parts; the shell is checked against the .scad with the other two added (+0.07 %). The checked-in cad/stl/occ_cover.stl contains all three (compared against the shell only, hence -12.5 %).
* **Totals.** MATERIALS.md edge-node and barrier stated totals (9 kg, 24 kg) are about 10 % and 11 % higher than the sum of their own listed rows (see sections above); gantry total is consistent.

## Limitations

* Fasteners, anchors, decals, tape and wiring are not modelled. Bought-in parts are simplified envelopes at assumed class sizes.
* Literals copied from .scad module bodies (not parameters): DIN device list, lane rig dimensions (2400, 700, 6800, 600, 2380), spreader bar length formula, 40 mm slot inset.
* Sign bracket is flat (no bends); tilt plate has sharp bends; sun hood is unbent; T-slot is a generic profile, not a vendor section.
* The occupancy cover keeps the .scad flaws (floating boss and seat); base keyhole counterbore is an enclosed void in the .scad.
* Densities for PC and EPDM are not in MATERIALS.md, so no mass is computed for them.

## History

The four STEP files that existed first (base_weldment, antenna_yoke, antenna_tilt_plate, antenna_bracket_assy) were regenerated. The first versions differed from the .scad (yoke cheek outline, arc slot direction, missing grout slots and cheek notches); the current files follow the .scad and carry the weldment at 1414.5 cm3 instead of 1424.8 cm3.
